newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS-Braathens, KLM announce air alliance.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Braathens, KLM announce air alliance.

text.p: Norwegian airline Braathens SAFE announced on Monday an alliance with KLM Royal Dutch Airline in a deal analysts said will open up competition in the Scandinavian sector.

Under the agreement, which was cemented after a year of secret talks, KLM will acquire around 30 percent of Oslo-based Braathens from majority shareholder Ludv. G. Braathens Rederi. Final terms of the deal have yet to be settled.

"Braathens SAFE and KLM expect that the close partnership will substantially strengthen the European market position and customer preference both for the Norwegian carrier and for KLM and its partners," Braathens said in a statement.
"Braathens' strong regional position coupled with the international network of KLM and its partners will strengthen the group's European market position," the company said.
KLM operates other alliances with America's Northwest Airlines and Britain's AirUK.

The mainly long-haul Dutch airline has made no secret of a desire to make strategic alliances to increase market share in Europe. Analysts said the Braathens deal came as a surprise as a link-up with Italy's Alitalia had been mooted.

"This is certainly the way forward in terms of consolidation with global partners tying up with local carriers where airlines like KLM cannot operate alone because of a high operating cost base," Kevin Fogarty at Daiwa Europe in London, told Reuters.
"In return Braathens can use a global carrier to extend its reach and also gain leverage of brand."
Braathens already is cooperating closely with Finland's Finnair and Maersk of Denmark. The company said it would continue with these alliances and intensify them in the future.
But, it said, most of its cooperation with British Airways (BP), including a bonus-point programme and a handling agreement, would be broken up once the KLM deal was in place.

"The cooperation (with BA) is not as extensive as people thought," said Erik Braathen, CEO at the airliner. "The bonus programme 'Frequent Flyer' will end but the handling agreement is a long-term agreement and will continue," he said.

Analysts said that in the short term, the cooperation was expected to relieve pressure on the region's main airline Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS). In the longer term, however, the Braathens/KLM pact and BA will likely squeeze SAS' domination, they said.

"This surely opens up the battle for Scandinavia," said an Oslo-based analyst. "There is now a new competitor in the Scandinavian market with Braathens/KLM and Northwest. The Braathens/BA alliance is now lost, but BA certainly won't be sidelined."
SAS said it saw no major change to its competitive position from the Braathens/KLM deal.
"We expected our own Star Alliance to set off changes in the airline sector. This is just one of a series of developments we expect in the future," said SAS chief spokesman Peter Forssman.

Braathens said the partnership will be implemented in phases and will include greater coordination of connecting services and a selection of connecting services through Schipol airport in Amsterdam using the KLM and partners' network.
The airlines are considering increasing the frequency of service between Norway and Schipol and intensifying cooperation between Braathens and AirUK on Norway-United Kingdom routes.
KLM and Northwest Airlines will focus on creating optimal connections between Scandinavian markets and the United States.
Braathens and KLM will also join forces in marketing and sales and examine potential for cooperation areas, including equipment and technical maintenance and purchasing.
They will also link Braathens' frequent flier programme, BRACard, and KLM's Flying Dutchman programme.
Both transactions have been submitted to relevant regulatory authorities for review. Braathens said the parties hoped to enter a final agreement within four to eight weeks.
